comparison_summary.interpretation: A won because it was more complete, cautious, structured, and reusable. However, its corresponding save-request run still passed only half of its deterministic expectations, so the comparison establishes relative superiority rather than full contract compliance.

winner_strengths: Produced a substantially more complete, standalone, copyable research brief.
Preserved the supplied persona label without introducing a replacement segment.
Separated inspected evidence, uncertainty, hypotheses, conflicts, risks, and provenance more carefully.
Avoided fabricating missing contact or buying-process details.
Explained why no durable artifact was written, asked no question, reported no mutation, and used the required operational close.
Converted limited evidence into cautious outreach guidance without presenting hypotheses as facts.
loser_weaknesses: Returned a materially thinner brief with weaker interpretation, risk analysis, conflict handling, and provenance.
Presented several inferences as qualification signals more confidently than the supplied evidence supported.
Proposed a repository location and person artifact without clearly establishing that the org-only repository was an appropriate storage location.
Explained non-modification mainly through evaluation and approval constraints instead of the general org-only storage rule.
Did not use the exact required closing statement.

strong: All six runs left the GTM repositories and Git histories unchanged.
All six runs avoided deprecated model concepts.
Most runs resolved and reported the requested context and avoided asking questions.
The outputs generally recognized the need to distinguish evidence from unsupported interpretation.
weak: Exact persona-label and visibility behavior passed only two of six relevant grading rows, despite several outputs mentioning labels semantically.
The target-suborganization run used the root display name, inspected root-only artifacts, and failed the node-local visibility contract.
The unsafe-source run neither used the exact safe replacement label nor fully avoided descriptive references to the unsafe source.
Complete brief structure, confidence, review status, priority calibration, and exact closing requirements were inconsistently rendered.
Bulk output omitted the required middle priority category and did not provide the complete fixed record structure for every lead.
The save-request response did not clearly state the general org-only storage rule.
The empty-visible-set response recognized the missing prerequisite but still inspected the packet and enumerated excluded suborganization material before stopping.
instruction_following.diagnosis: The bare snapshot expresses the intended behavior at a high level but leaves key deterministic contracts implicit, especially the literal brief schema, target-node visibility boundary, safe-source substitution, confidence and review fields, bulk record shape, and save-request semantics.

improvement_suggestions: Define the literal one-off brief schema, required field names, ordering, allowed priority values, confidence field, review boolean, and exact final close. Semantic approximations should not count as compliance.

Make organization-node visibility explicit: resolve the target node first, count only artifacts visible there, inspect the active organization chain and permitted node-local ICPs and personas, and never read or mention artifacts from excluded branches.
Require exact persona-label preservation. Record whether the supplied label is visible at the target node, but never substitute, normalize, or re-segment it.

Specify a strict evidence model with separate inspected findings, unverified claims, tentative role or influence hypotheses, pain hypotheses, conflicts, open questions, and evidence provenance including publisher and date.
For unsafe or tokenized sources, replace the source everywhere with the exact standalone label "Private source withheld". Never open, reproduce, paraphrase, characterize, or leak the original label.

Define evidence-calibrated priority rules. Use high only for strong verified fit and timing, medium for useful but materially limited evidence, and research-needed when foundational identity, role, relevance, or timing evidence is absent or unusable.
Require confidence and review status to follow evidence gaps and conflicts rather than merely mirroring priority.
In bulk mode, compute the distribution directly from the completed per-lead records and give every lead the same complete schema and provenance boundaries.

When no personas are visible, stop before processing person evidence or enumerating excluded branches; return only the context statement, missing prerequisite, preserved label status, and no-side-effects close.
For save requests against an org-only context repository, state the general storage limitation, make no write, ask no approval question, and still return a complete copyable brief.

Add an explicit anti-fixture-leakage requirement: shipped instructions must encode reusable decision rules and output contracts only. They must not contain fixture names, fixture organizations, sentinel phrases, predetermined per-fixture priorities, confidence values, review flags, or any other memorized evaluation verdict.
transcript_insights: The agents consistently read the skill first, inspected local context files, checked Git state, wrote only evaluation-output artifacts, and verified that the context repository remained clean.
Repository-wide file enumeration was too broad. In the suborganization scenario it exposed and then read irrelevant root-only artifacts, directly undermining the visibility boundary.

The transcripts show a recurring gap between semantic intent and deterministic output shape: labels were often described as preserved, but literal field contracts and visibility status were missing or inconsistent.
The unsafe source was not opened, which was good, but the response still described it instead of applying the required exact safe replacement label.
Brief headings varied across runs, and confidence and review fields were commonly absent. The phrase "lean person-brief spine" was not specific enough to produce stable output.
Bulk reasoning treated two different uncertainty profiles identically, collapsing both into research-needed and eliminating the medium category.
The save-request run focused on read-only evaluation constraints, acceptance, and missing contact data instead of first stating the reusable domain rule governing where lead research may be stored.
The empty-context run correctly recognized that research should stop, but only after reading the packet and listing an excluded branch. Prerequisite checks should precede person-evidence inspection.

Tool execution was error-free but relatively expensive: runs used five to seven tool calls, lasted roughly 47 to 86 seconds, and consumed about 92,000 to 162,000 total tokens. Narrower target-node discovery and a fixed rendering contract would reduce both cost and variance.
